# Platform Overview, Licensing, and Community Maturity

Covers dimensions 1 (What it is), 2 (Licensing), and 12 (Community and maturity).
All citations reference entries in [citations.md](../citations.md).

---

## What Tines Is

Tines is a no-code workflow automation platform originally built for security
operations (SOAR), now expanding to general IT and business workflows [1][2].
Founded in 2018 in Dublin by Eoin Hinchy (CEO) and Thomas Kinsella (now Chief
Customer Officer), both with 10+ years in senior security roles at eBay,
DocuSign, and Deloitte [1][2]. Hinchy notably managed DocuSign's response to
a 145 million user record breach [2].

The platform's mission is "to power the world's most important workflows" [1].
Users build automated processes ("stories") via a drag-and-drop interface
without coding expertise, connecting to any service with an API [2].

### Architecture

| Component | Description | Source |
|-----------|-------------|--------|
| Core model | Event-driven "stories" composed of "actions" | [2] |
| Web server | tines-app (Rails) | [9] |
| Background worker | tines-sidekiq (async via Redis) | [9] |
| SSL termination | tines-nginx (or any reverse proxy) | [9] |
| Data layer | PostgreSQL (persistent) + Redis (queue/cache) | [9] |
| Communication | Async task queuing via Redis; no direct container-to-container | [9] |

Eight action types handle different automation steps (email, HTTP requests,
data transformation, triggers, etc.) [2]. Actions output events that feed
into subsequent actions in the story [2].

### Key Product Components

- **Stories**: Visual workflows composed of actions [2]
- **Cases**: Collaborative incident tracking workspace [2]
- **Records**: Structured data capture from workflow runs [2]
- **Dashboards**: Real-time metrics and performance analytics [2]
- **Workbench**: Generative AI chat interface for querying data and taking
  action [4]
- **Story Library**: Pre-built workflow templates organized by team/use case [50]

## Licensing

Tines is **proprietary, closed-source software** [29]. There is no open-source
edition and no source code access. This contrasts with n8n (Sustainable Use
License, source-available) and alternatives like Temporal (MIT), Windmill
(AGPLv3), or Kestra (Apache-2.0).

### Pricing Tiers

| Tier | Price | Builders | Flows | Events | AI Credits | Self-Host |
|------|-------|----------|-------|--------|------------|-----------|
| Community | $0 | 1 | 3 | 25K/mo | 50/mo | No |
| Starter | $500/mo | 2 | 5 | 1M/mo | 2,500/mo | No |
| Business | Contact sales | 100 | 30 | 1.5M/day | 10K/mo | Yes |
| Enterprise | Contact sales | Unlimited | 150 | 10M/day | 100K/mo | Yes |

Source: [5]

The pricing model is **feature-tier based with usage allocations**, not
per-action charges [6]. Capacity can be increased via add-ons (AI credits,
tunnels, tenants, flows, teams, cases) without changing tier [6]. Enhanced
packaging was introduced June 25, 2025 [6].

### Community Edition Details

The Community Edition provides [5][7]:
- 1 builder, unlimited viewers
- 3 flows (stories), 25,000 monthly events
- 50 monthly AI credits (non-rollover, no top-up) [25]
- Workbench: 20 daily messages tenant-wide [7]
- SSO, unlimited integrations, unlimited parallel runs [5]
- MCP server template included [24]
- **No self-hosting** [5][8]

Event retention on Community is 24 hours [5].

### Personal Use Implications

The Community Edition is viable for personal experimentation, PoCs, and
learning [7]. The 3-flow limit and 25K monthly event cap constrain production
use. The jump from free to Starter ($500/mo) is steep for personal use.
Self-hosting is only available at Business tier and above, requiring sales
contact [5][8].

### Company Size and Growth

- Founded 2018, Dublin [1]
- Headquarters: Dublin and Boston [2]
- Employee count: estimated 350-476 (multiple conflicting third-party sources) [2]
- Revenue: not publicly disclosed; growth rates disclosed as multiples [2]
- ARR doubled year-over-year through 2023-2024 [2]
- 80-90% of revenue from North America (as of 2021) [2]
- 400+ customers by June 2025 [2]
- Over 1 billion automated tasks weekly [3][4]
- Two-thirds of customers using AI features (as of Feb 2025) [4]

### Notable Customers

Coinbase, Databricks, GitLab, Mars, Reddit, Canva, Elastic, Kayak, Intercom,
McKesson, HashiCorp, Oak Ridge National Laboratory [3][2].

### GitHub Presence

Tines maintains repositories under @tines and @tines-io GitHub organizations,
but with minimal community engagement. Notable repositories have low star
counts (terraform-provider-tines: ~13 stars, go-sdk: ~6 stars) [2]. This is
a proprietary platform — GitHub repos are for API clients and tooling, not
the core product.

### Release Cadence

8-week major release cycle for self-hosted versions [27]. Recent releases
show weekly incremental updates (v39.3.0 through v40.1.0 between March 3-31,
2026) [27]. Notable recent additions include MCP servers with OAuth, Mistral
model support, and record CSV import [27].

### Industry Recognition

- Gartner Cool Vendor in Security Operations, 2021 [2]
- $1.125B unicorn valuation (Feb 2025) [3]

### Market Positioning

Tines positions itself in the security automation market ($9.1B in 2023,
projected $27.8B by 2032 at 13.3% CAGR) [2]. Key competitors include Torq,
Palo Alto Networks Cortex XSOAR, Splunk Phantom, Swimlane, Google Security
Operations, Microsoft Sentinel, IBM QRadar SOAR, and ServiceNow Security
Operations [2].

Over 25% of customers now use Tines outside security [2], reflecting a
strategic pivot toward general IT/business workflow automation [41].

## Gaps and Limitations

- **No open source option** — fully proprietary with no source access [29]
- **Revenue not publicly disclosed** — third-party estimates conflict
  significantly [2]
- **Employee count uncertain** — sources range from ~350 to ~476 [2]
- **GitHub community is minimal** — not a community-driven project [2]
- **Geographic revenue concentration** — 80-90% North America as of 2021 [2]
